items.text: Sheaves on $\operatorname{Spec}A$ via the open sets $X_f$
A sheaf on $X$ = a sheaf on a basis of opens: a contravariant functor $X_f\mapsto F(X_f)$ such that, for every covering $X_f=\bigcup X_{f_i}$ (with $X_{f_i}\cap X_{f_j}=X_{f_if_j}$),
F(X_f)\longrightarrow\prod_i F(X_{f_i})\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}F(X_{f_if_j})\quad\text{exact}
Data: for each $f\in A$ a set (group, ring, ...) $G(f)=G(X_f)$; for $X_f\subset X_g$ a restriction map
\rho_{fg}\colon G(g)\to G(f),\qquad \rho_{fh}=\rho_{fg}\rho_{gh},\ \ \rho_{ff}=\mathrm{id}
Translating $X_f\subset X_g$ into algebra
X_f\subset X_g\iff V(g)\subset V(f)\iff f\in\sqrt{gA}\iff\exists\,n\ge0,\ h\in A:\ f^n=gh
This relation is transitive: a preorder on $A$ (a power of $f$ is divisible by $g$).
X_f=\bigcup_i X_{f_i}\iff\begin{cases}\forall i\ \exists\, n_i,h_i:\ f_i^{n_i}=fh_i&(X_{f_i}\subset X_f)\\ \exists\, n,\ g_i\in A:\ f^n=\sum_i g_if_i&(V(f)\supset\bigcap V(f_i))\end{cases}
The site of the opens $X_f$ (category plus coverings) expressed in algebra.
The sheaf $\widetilde M$
$M$ an $A$-module; set $\widetilde M(f)=M_f$ (when $M=A$: a sheaf of rings $\widetilde A$, and $\widetilde M$ a sheaf of $\widetilde A$-modules).
The localised module $M_f$
M_f=\varinjlim\bigl(M\xrightarrow{\,f\,}M\xrightarrow{\,f\,}M\to\cdots\bigr)

On $M_f$ multiplication by $f$ is bijective: surjective (an element of the limit comes from some $M_\alpha$, then is $f\cdot$ its image in $M_{\alpha+1}$); injective (if $fx=0$ then $x$ dies in $M_{\alpha+1}$).
Universal property. $M\to M_f$ is universal among $A$-homomorphisms $M\to N$ with $f$ bijective on $N$: it factors uniquely through $M_f$. Hence $M\mapsto M_f$ is functorial.
Fractions: elements $x/f^n$ ($x\in M$), with
\lambda\cdot\frac x{f^n}=\frac{\lambda x}{f^n},\qquad \frac x{f^n}+\frac y{f^{n'}}=\frac{f^{n'}x+f^ny}{f^{n+n'}}
\frac x{f^n}=\frac{x'}{f^{n'}}\iff\exists\,m:\ f^m\bigl(f^{n'}x-f^nx'\bigr)=0\ \text{in }M
$M\to M_f$, $x\mapsto x/1$. For $M=A$: the ring $A_f$, with $\dfrac x{f^n}\cdot\dfrac y{f^{n'}}=\dfrac{xy}{f^{n+n'}}$.
$M_f$ is an $A_f$-module: $\dfrac\lambda{f^n}\cdot\dfrac x{f^m}=\dfrac{\lambda x}{f^{n+m}}$.
$A_f$ is universal for ring homomorphisms $A\to R$ ($R$ any ring) inverting $f$; hence an $A_f$-module = an $A$-module on which $f$ acts bijectively.
Restriction maps
$X_f\subset X_g$ (so $f^n=gh$): $g$ acts invertibly on $M_f$ (since $f^n$ does), so $M\to M_f$ factors uniquely through $M_g$:
\rho_{fg}\colon M_g\to M_f,\ \text{functorial in }M,\ \text{transitive}
Main statement. $f\mapsto M_f$ is a sheaf on the site of the $X_f$: for $X_f=\bigcup X_{f_i}$,
$\widetilde A$ is a presheaf of rings, $\widetilde M$ a presheaf of $\widetilde A$-modules (compatible restrictions $A_f\to A_g$).
0\to M_f\to\prod_i M_{f_i}\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}M_{f_if_j}\quad\text{exact}
Injectivity
Replacing $f_i$ by powers (same $X_{f_i}$) assume $f\mid f_i$: $f_i=fh_i$. Suppose $x/f^n\mapsto0$ in every $M_{f_i}$:
\frac x{f^n}=\frac{xh_i^n}{f_i^n}=0\ \text{in }M_{f_i}\iff\exists\, m:\ f_i^m\,xh_i^n=0\ \Longrightarrow\ f_i^{n+m}x=0
Replacing $f_i$ by $f_i^{n+m}$: $f_ix=0$ for all $i$. (A finite subcover suffices, so infinitely many indices cause no problem.)
f^N=\sum_ig_if_i\ \Longrightarrow\ f^Nx=\sum_ig_if_ix=0,\ \text{so}\ \frac x{f^n}=0
